facts.raw_span: intermittent palpitations for 2 days
no history of chest pain, dyspnea, congestion, or fever
no past cardiac history or family history of similar complaints
Blood pressure was 110/72 mm Hg
respiratory rate was 14 bpm
Cardiovascular system examination results were unremarkable
Wide complex tachycardia at rate of 190 bpm
atypical left bundle branch morphology (QS in leads V1-V5 with transition in V6)
QRS duration of 146 ms with no evidence of AV dissociation
Global hypokinesia of right ventricle, dilated RV, ballooned out RVOT measuring 35 mm
RV ejection fraction of 19.3%
Postcontrast hyperenhancement along RV free wall, RVOT apical wall, RV aspect of septum, and in basal inferior, midcavity inferior, and inferoseptal myocardium of left ventricle

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of wide complex tachycardia, global hypokinesia of the right ventricle, and postcontrast hyperenhancement along the RV free wall are consistent with ARVC.
The patient's ECG showing wide complex tachycardia at a rate of 190 bpm is consistent with VT.
The patient's ECG and echocardiography results showing a ballooned out RVOT are consistent with RVOT Tachycardia.
The patient's echocardiography and cardiac MRI results showing a dilated right ventricle and low RV ejection fraction are consistent with DCM.
It explains the atypical left bundle branch morphology found in the ECG studies.

rationales.F07: Wide complex tachycardia is more common in ventricular tachycardia and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F08: Atypical left bundle branch morphology is characteristic of left bundle branch block.
rationales.F09: QRS duration and absence of AV dissociation are typical of ventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F10: Global hypokinesia and dilated right ventricle are characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F11: Low RV ejection fraction is typical of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F12: Postcontrast hyperenhancement along the right ventricular free wall is characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The combination of wide complex tachycardia, global hypokinesia of the right ventricle, dilated RV, and postcontrast hyperenhancement along the RV free wall strongly supports Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy, which explains the majority of the findings without strong contradiction.
